title: Isolated retry-level physical-solver forensics across deterministic G21G status islands
bounded_conclusions: The deterministic G21G status islands are reproduced at retry level: for both representative boundaries, the status-6 head has physical-solver convergence at retry levels 0 through 7 followed by temporal rejection at each level, then physical-solver nonconvergence at retry level 8.
The immediately adjacent status-0 head converges physically at retry level 8, after the same earlier temporal-rejection ladder.

This confirms that the full-transaction status-6 versus status-0 split is caused by a physical-solver bifurcation at the smallest retry duration in these frozen boundaries, not by hidden transaction-history dependence.

The larger-duration attempts are not physical-solver failures. They are solver-converged attempts rejected by the temporal model certificate, with normalized indicator still above one through retry level 7.

At the status-6 final retry the solver consumes 16 nonlinear iterations, 16 Jacobian builds and 16 linear solves; the two frozen failing heads show different backtracking counts (104 and 39), so the next causal question lies inside the physical nonlinear-solver trajectory rather than in the transaction ladder.
The isolated diagnostic does not mutate saved corrector configuration, accepted SWAP state, ledger authority, participant candidate state or G16 publication authority.

This is diagnostic mechanism evidence only. It does not justify smoothing the binary64 status islands, changing retry depth, temporal tolerances, physical-solver tolerances, solver configuration, or production globalization policy.
next_natural_unit: Preregister a G21I final-retry physical-solver trajectory forensic across the same adjacent 6->0 and 0->6 heads. Capture read-only per-Newton-iteration residual, update, backtracking and convergence diagnostics at duration 3.90625e-5 day to identify the numerical branch that causes the 16-iteration failure only on the status-6 side.
